skills.name: AI Content Detector
skills.description: Estimate whether text (or a web page's text) is AI-written using a trained classifier: about 78% accurate on a held-out benchmark (not a guarantee). Uncertain results suggest a rerun on a longer section (300+ words); tell phrases are only a secondary 'possible AI influence' signal.

example_request.text: So I finally fixed the porch light on Saturday. It's worth noting that I'd tried twice before and gave up (the wiring is ancient). Honestly the whole thing was a testament to stubbornness. My brother Sam held the ladder and complained the entire time, which didn't help one bit. In conclusion, the bulb works, the switch clicks, and I only shocked myself once! Next up is the doorbell, if I can find the manual. I can't, probably. It's in a box somewhere in the garage behind 3 bikes and a broken lawnmower.

evidence: rhythm is in the overlap range where human and prompted-AI text both sit
tells: it's worth noting, a testament to, in conclusion
surprisal mean 3.21, variance 2.15, spike 0.40; rare-word share 0.033; MATTR 0.834; Zipf slope deviation 0.63
tell phrases are dense; possible AI influence (secondary signal)
first person, names, dialogue and sensory detail are not counted either way
tell phrases present but not confirmed by two sections; secondary signal only

caveats: Detection is probabilistic and should not be used as the only evidence that a text was or was not written by a person.
ai_likelihood is a stylometric score from 0 to 1, not a calibrated probability. The band widens when there is less text and is not a statistical confidence interval.
A low score means these surface patterns are weak. It does not prove a person wrote the text.
Weights were chosen on a small set of public-domain prose, poems, and synthetic assistant-style paragraphs. Fixture accuracy is not a field accuracy.
